title: SIGSEGV after auto-update to v2.0.15 on Synology-NAS armv7l

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> Oh, interesting [@participant2](https://github.com/participant2) ! The `syncthing` binary at `/volume1/@appdata/syncthing/bin` (which SIGSEGV's, so cannot report its own version) has an MD5SUM of `f4aa4515c3a95befe4598e7af29aa038` and is 25224164 bytes in size. Not sure if that's enough to identify it?

Yup, that's v2.0.15:

```
f4aa4515c3a95befe4598e7af29aa038  syncthing-linux-arm-v2.0.15/syncthing
```

So your installation indeed auto-upgraded. You can disable auto-upgrades by setting the environment variable `STNOUPGRADE=1`, but I assume that's not easily done when using a Synology package.

Instead, you could try editing the Syncthing config file and setting `options.autoUpgradeIntervalH` to `0`, i.e.:

```xml
<configuration version="XXX">
  <!-- [stuff omitted] -->
  <options>
    <!-- [stuff omitted] -->
    <autoUpgradeIntervalH>0</autoUpgradeIntervalH>
    <!-- [stuff omitted] -->
  </options>
  <!-- [stuff omitted] -->
</configuration>
```

Then replace the `syncthing` binary with the old, working version (there's likely a binary named `synthing.old` next to the current one, so just rename that to `syncthing`), and things should work again.

Oh, and remember to remove this setting after the bug is fixed (or maybe leave it in-place since updates are supposed to be handled by the package manager).

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
That's exactly what I did. Setting `autoUpgradeIntervalH` to `0` in the config and reverting to the old executable.

> Oh, and remember to remove this setting after the bug is fixed (or maybe leave it in-place since updates are supposed to be handled by the package manager).

The `syncthing` package for Synology is provided by the SynoCommunity and is only updated to accommodate breaking changes. Otherwise, it depends on the auto-update.

But you can still manually upgrade via the button in the Web UI even if the auto-update is disabled by setting `autoUpgradeIntervalH` to `0`.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body: Note for anyone else attempting to manually download and replace their Synology version of Syncthing: There is a `/volume1/@appdata/syncthing/bin` folder that has a copy of the Syncthing binary, but that is not the one that actually gets triggered through the web UI when you launch the Syncthing package. The one you want to replace is at `/volume1/@appstore/syncthing/bin`. Those file paths look very similar (difference is `@participant13` instead of `@participant14`), so took me a while in the logs to figure out why replacing the one at `/volume1/@appdata/syncthing/bin` wasn't allowing the service to start up again... 🔍

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
> Looks like this will be fixed in golang v1.26.3, when it's released: [golang/go#77931 (comment)](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/77931#issuecomment-4308039273)

~Now it looks like all we need is for the source code to be updated to use it. It should only require a change to this line:~
https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/blob/5dd22cfd85020d394abb1521a3943767d876e165/go.mod#L3

EDIT: Alternately, if we don't want to change that line we can add one like this just below it:
```
toolchain go1.26.3
```

EDIT: Based on this repo's infra config, it will use the newer Go v1.26.3 automatically on the next release. In the meantime, I've used the `toolchain` directive to patch the SynoCommunity build for the existing version in https://github.com/SynoCommunity/spksrc/pull/7130. Feel free to test and provide feedback.

comments.author: participant11
comments.body: Folks, following successful testing, the package update with the explicit `toolchain` directive (from https://github.com/SynoCommunity/spksrc/pull/7130) has been published to the SynoCommunity [website](https://synocommunity.com/package/syncthing). You can manually download and install or update from the Package Center in a day or so (after the global caches update). This should resolve the issue identified in this ticket.
